claim: Positional information is a central concept in developmental biology.
source: Positional information is a central concept in developmental biology.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus in the field of developmental biology.

claim: In developing organs, positional information can be idealized as a local coordinate system that arises from morphogen gradients controlled by organizers at key locations.
source: In developing organs, positional information can be idealized as a local coordinate system that arises from morphogen gradients controlled by organizers at key locations.
evidence: This represents a conceptual framework based on established developmental biology theory.

claim: Positional information offers a plausible mechanism for the integration of molecular networks operating in individual cells into spatially coordinated multicellular responses necessary for the organization of emergent forms.
source: This offers a plausible mechanism for the integration of the molecular networks operating in individual cells into the spatially coordinated multicellular responses necessary for the organization of emergent forms.
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation based on developmental biology principles.

claim: MorphoGraphX software implements a generalized framework to annotate developing organs with local coordinate systems.
source: Here, we present recent advances in the MorphoGraphX software (Barbier de Reuille et al., 2015⁠) that implement a generalized framework to annotate developing organs with local coordinate systems.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software presented in this manuscript.

claim: Local coordinate systems introduce an organ-centric spatial context to microscopy data.
source: These coordinate systems introduce an organ-centric spatial context to microscopy data, allowing gene expression and growth to be quantified and compared in the context of the positional information thought to control them.
evidence: This describes the functionality of the coordinate system framework implemented in the software.

claim: Many aspects of animal morphogenesis are thought to be controlled by positional information.
source: Many aspects of animal morphogenesis are thought to be controlled by positional information (Wolpert, 1969)⁠
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wolpert, 1969.

claim: Positional information may be even more pervasive in plants than in animals because plant cells cannot relocate within organs and must decide their fate based on their location.
source: This phenomenon may be even more pervasive in plants as cells cannot relocate within organs and must decide their fate based on their location.
evidence: This is an inference based on the biological constraint that plant cells are immobile.

claim: Root morphogenesis appears to be controlled by an organizing center at the root tip that provides founder cells and positional information to the growing structure.
source: For example, root morphogenesis appears to be controlled by an organizing center at the root tip that provides founder cells and positional information to the growing structure (Scheres et al., 2002)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Scheres et al., 2002.

claim: Ablation of cortical cell initials in the root meristem causes neighboring pericycle cells to divide and fill the available space, subsequently adopting the fate associated with their new location.
source: Ablation of cortical cell initials in the root meristem causes the neighboring pericycle cells to divide and fill the available space, subsequently adopting the fate associated to their new location (van den Berg et al., 1995)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to van den Berg et al., 1995.

claim: A similar effect of cells adopting fate based on location has been demonstrated for a variety of cell types in the Arabidopsis root.
source: A similar effect has been demonstrated for a variety of cell types in the Arabidopsis root (Marhava et al., 2019)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Marhava et al., 2019.

claim: In leaves, development is thought to be coordinated by polarity fields oriented from leaf base to tip.
source: In leaves, development is thought to be coordinated by polarity fields oriented from leaf base to tip (Kierzkowski et al., 2019; Kuchen et al., 2012)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kierzkowski et al., 2019 and Kuchen et al., 2012.

claim: Over time organs can initiate new growth axes, such as when serrations or leaflets develop in more complex leaves.
source: Over time organs can initiate new growth axes, such as when serrations or leaflets develop in more complex leaves (Barkoulas et al., 2008; Kierzkowski et al., 2019)⁠
evidence: This is supported by citations to Barkoulas et al., 2008 and Kierzkowski et al., 2019.

claim: Lateral roots emerge from the primary root as new growth axes.
source: or lateral roots emerge from the primary root (Scheres et al., 2002)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Scheres et al., 2002.

claim: New software packages for cell segmentation and lineage tracking are being developed as computational power and imaging methods improve.
source: As computational power and imaging methods improve, new software packages for cell segmentation and lineage tracking are being developed (Sommer et al., 2011; Stegmaier et al., 2016⁠)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sommer et al., 2011 and Stegmaier et al., 2016.

claim: Many software packages for cell segmentation and lineage tracking are specialized for plants.
source: including many specialized for plants (Barbier de Reuille et al., 2015; Eschweiler et al., 2019; Fernandez et al., 2010; Schmidt et al., 2014; Wolny et al., 2020)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple plant-specific software packages.

claim: Progress in segmentation tools has enabled the segmentation of time-lapse data at increasingly higher resolution and throughput.
source: This progress has enabled the segmentation of time-lapse data at increasingly higher resolution and throughput (Hervieux et al., 2016; Kierzkowski et al., 2019; Sapala et al., 2018; Willis et al., 2016)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies demonstrating high-resolution time-lapse segmentation.

claim: The analysis of geometric data from thousands of cells is nontrivial.
source: Although this increase in data volume offers tremendous potential to understand how genes control form, the analysis of geometric data from thousands of cells is nontrivial.
evidence: This is a statement about the computational challenge of analyzing large datasets.

claim: Information about a cell's shape, gene expression, and growth directions is of limited value when the cell's spatial context within the developing organ is unknown.
source: Information about a cell's shape, gene expression, and growth directions is of limited value when the cell's spatial context within the developing organ is unknown.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the importance of spatial context for interpreting cellular data.

claim: MorphoGraphX is a computer software platform that is specialized for image processing on surface layers of cells.
source: MorphoGraphX is a computer software platform that is specialized for image processing on surface layers of cells (Barbier de Reuille et al., 2015)⁠.
evidence: This describes the software and is supported by a citation to the original publication.

claim: MorphoGraphX has proven especially useful for the analysis of confocal microscopy images from time-lapse data to quantify cellular-level dynamics of growth, cell division, and gene expression.
source: It has proven especially useful for the analysis of confocal microscopy images from time-lapse data in order to quantify the cellular-level dynamics of growth, cell division, and gene expression (e.g., Bringmann and Bergmann, 2017; Feng et al., 2018; Hervieux et al., 2016; Hong et al., 2016; Kierzkowski et al., 2019; Louveaux et al., 2016; Sapala et al., 2018; Scheuring et al., 2016; Tsugawa et al., 2017; Vlad et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2020; Zhu et al., 2020; Fridman et al., 2021)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies that have used MorphoGraphX.

claim: MorphoGraphX represents cell layers as curved, triangulated surface meshes that capture the overall 3D shape of organs.
source: Key to the approach taken in the software is the representation of cell layers as curved, triangulated surface meshes that capture the overall 3D shape of organs, which retains much of the simplicity of 2D segmentation and lineage tracking.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the software's approach.

claim: The '2.5D' images in MorphoGraphX contain the geometry of the sample at two scales: the global shape of the organ is captured by the mesh's geometry, while a cellular-scale representation is obtained from the confocal signal projected onto the mesh.
source: These '2.5D' images contain the geometry of the sample at two scales. The global shape of the organ is captured by the mesh's geometry, while a cellular-scale representation is obtained from the confocal signal projected onto the mesh, which is segmented to extract the shape of individual cells on the surface (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This describes the multi-scale representation in the software and references Figure 1A-C for visual evidence.

claim: When combined with time-lapse data acquisition and cell lineage tracking, MorphoGraphX allows cell growth and its relationship to gene expression to be quantified.
source: When combined with time-lapse data acquisition and cell lineage tracking, MorphoGraphX allows cell growth and its relationship to gene expression to be quantified (Figure 1D and E; Kierzkowski et al., 2019; Sapala et al., 2018; Vlad et al., 2014)⁠.
evidence: This describes a capability of the software, supported by figure references and citations.

claim: MorphoGraphX supports the creation and analysis of full 3D meshes with volumetric cells.
source: In addition to cell surface analysis, MorphoGraphX also supports the creation and analysis of full 3D meshes with volumetric cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Vijayan et al., 2021)⁠.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software, supported by a figure reference and citation.

claim: The simplest method to provide positional information for cells in a sample is by aligning the sample with a set of 3D coordinate axes.
source: The simplest method to provide positional information for the cells in a sample is by aligning the sample with a set of 3D coordinate axes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes a method implemented in the software and references Figure 2A.

claim: For curved organs, the central axis can be defined by a curved line that conforms to the curvature of the organ.
source: However, for curved organs significant errors will occur, especially in more distal regions, further from the origin. In this case, the central axis can be defined by a curved line that conforms to the curvature of the organ (Figure 2C; Schmidt et al., 2014; Montenegro-Johnson et al., 2015)⁠.
evidence: This describes a method for handling curved organs, supported by a figure reference and citations.

claim: In MorphoGraphX, curved lines can be represented by Bezier splines with control points positioned using interactive manipulation or automatically from a selected file of cells.
source: In MorphoGraphX, this line can be represented by a Bezier spline (Bézier, 1968)⁠ with control points positioned using either interactive manipulation or automatically from a selected file of cells.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software, with a citation to the Bezier spline method.

claim: MorphoGraphX allows a 2D Bezier surface to be positioned next to or within a sample, enabling two directions to be aligned with the natural curvature of the sample.
source: MorphoGraphX also allows a 2D Bezier surface to be positioned next to or within a sample, enabling two directions to be aligned with the natural curvature of the sample.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software.

claim: An alternative method to create a distance field is to select one or more cells at a reference position and calculate the distance relative to the selection.
source: An alternative method is to select one or more cells at a reference position and calculate the distance relative to the selection (Figure 2D, Video 1).
evidence: This describes a method implemented in the software, with references to Figure 2D and Video 1.

claim: The distance in the cell-based distance field is determined by computing the shortest path along cells through the tissue, causing it to naturally follow the curvature of the organ.
source: The distance is determined by computing the shortest path along cells through the tissue, causing it to naturally follow the curvature of the organ.
evidence: This describes how the distance calculation works in the software.

claim: Initially growth in the Arabidopsis sepal is predominantly located at the distal parts of the organ, followed by progressive displacement of the high growth zone towards the base.
source: On the full 7-day sepal time-lapse shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 (Hervieux et al., 2016)⁠, initially growth is predominantly located at the distal parts of the organ, followed by the progressive displacement of the high growth zone towards the base of the sepal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis shown in the figure, with a citation to the data source.

claim: By time point 6 in the sepal time-lapse, growth has slowed and become more uniform as the organ differentiates.
source: By time point 6, the growth has slowed and become more uniform as the organ differentiates.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis.

claim: Proliferation in the Arabidopsis sepal is initially more uniform but follows a pattern similar to growth, progressing basally as the organ matures.
source: Proliferation is initially more uniform, but otherwise follows a pattern similar to growth, progressing basally as the organ matures (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Although the sepal appears to undergo a similar growth arrest starting at the tip as the Arabidopsis leaf, there are subtle differences.
source: It can be seen in the graphs that although the sepal appears to undergo a similar growth arrest starting at the tip as the Arabidopsis leaf, there are subtle differences.
evidence: This is a comparative observation based on data analysis.

claim: Growth in the early stages is more distal in the sepal compared to the Arabidopsis leaf, along with the proliferation, and the zone of higher growth moves towards the base as the sepal develops.
source: The growth in the early stages is more distal in the sepal, along with the proliferation, and the zone of higher growth moves towards the base as the sepal develops.
evidence: This is a comparative observation based on data analysis.

claim: In the Arabidopsis leaf, the growth and proliferation zones remain relatively fixed with respect to the total leaf length.
source: This is in contrast to the Arabidopsis leaf where the growth and proliferation zones remain relatively fixed with respect to the total leaf length (Figure 1K and M; Kierzkowski et al., 2019)⁠.
evidence: This is a comparative observation supported by a figure reference and citation.

claim: MorphoGraphX can quantify directional information such as the principal directions of growth (PDGs) that represent the maximal and minimal directions of growth for each cell.
source: In addition to scalar information such as areal growth rate or cell volume, MorphoGraphX can also quantify directional information, such as the principal directions of growth (PDGs) that represent the maximal and minimal directions of growth for each cell (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This describes a capability of the software with reference to Figure 3A-C.

claim: A common problem with the interpretation of directional information is the tendency for directions to be locally heterogeneous when growth is nearly isotropic.
source: A common problem with the interpretation of such directional information is the tendency for directions to be locally heterogeneous when growth is nearly isotropic.
evidence: This describes a known issue in the analysis of directional growth data.

claim: When growth is nearly isotropic, the maximal and minimal growth amounts are almost the same, and the displayed directions become arbitrary and heavily influenced by noise.
source: This happens because the maximal and minimal growth amounts are almost the same, and the displayed directions become arbitrary and heavily influenced by noise.
evidence: This explains why directional information can be problematic in isotropic growth.

claim: Growth directions can be projected onto a developmental axis and separated into components that are parallel and perpendicular to the axis.
source: The growth directions are then projected onto this developmental axis and separated into components that are parallel (Figure 3D) and perpendicular (Figure 3E) to the axis.
evidence: This describes a method implemented in the software with references to figures.

claim: In the A. thaliana leaf primordium, area extension differs greatly between midrib/petiole (low) and leaf blade cells (high), mainly due to differences in ML growth rate, whereas the PD growth map is more similar in these domains.
source: Using this method on the Arabidopsis thaliana leaf primordium different developmental zones with varying growth rates along the PD and medial-lateral (ML) axis can be revealed (Figure 3C–E): while the area extension differs greatly in midrib/petiole (low) and leaf blade cells (high), it can be seen that those differences mainly follow from the ML growth rate, whereas the PD growth map is more similar in these domains.
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis shown in the figures.

claim: An increase in ML growth around the forming serration can be seen in the A. thaliana leaf, separating it from surrounding leaf blade cells that show less growth along this direction.
source: Moreover, an increase in ML growth around the forming serration can be seen, separating it from the surrounding leaf blade cells that show less growth along this direction (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: From the original PDG visualization, it is not immediately apparent that the varying ML growth is the main cause of the differences in the domains.
source: From the original PDG visualization, it is not immediately apparent that the varying ML growth is the main cause of the differences in the domains (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a comparative observation about the utility of different visualization methods.

claim: Using local coordinate systems to analyze PDGs can provide a more direct comparison to the outputs of computational simulations.
source: Another benefit of looking at PDGs in the context of a local coordinate system is that it can provide a more direct comparison to the outputs of computational simulations.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the method for model comparison.

claim: Developmental models of emergent organ shape often use morphogens that are thought to specifically control growth in parallel and perpendicular to a developmental axis.
source: Developmental models of emergent organ shape often use morphogens that are thought to specifically control growth in parallel and perpendicular to a developmental axis (Kierzkowski et al., 2019; Kuchen et al., 2012; Whitewoods et al., 2020)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by citations to modeling studies.

claim: By projecting the PDGs onto a developmental axis, it is possible to directly compare model growth rates in different directions to experiments.
source: By projecting the PDGs onto this axis, it is possible to directly compare model growth rates in the different directions to experiments.
evidence: This describes a capability enabled by the method.

claim: MorphoGraphX can load a wide variety of mesh formats, allowing direct comparison of quantifications made on templates extracted from model simulations from various sources.
source: Since MorphoGraphX can load a wide variety of mesh formats, this allows the direct comparison of similar quantifications made on templates extracted from model simulations from various sources.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software that facilitates model-experiment comparison.

claim: For both primordia in the tomato meristem, radial growth has a high negative correlation with DR5 signal intensity.
source: For both primordia, we found radial growth to have a high negative correlation with DR5 signal intensity.
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis on the tomato meristem.

claim: In the tomato meristem, radial growth peaks on the abaxial side of the emerging primordium, whereas the DR5 signal is higher on the adaxial side.
source: Figure 3J shows that the radial growth (red) peaks on the abaxial side of the emerging primordium, whereas the DR5 signal (blue) is higher on the adaxial side.
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Circumferential growth in the tomato meristem primordia was more or less constant.
source: Circumferential growth was more or less constant.
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis.

claim: The DR5 maximum tends to be on the adaxial side of the initiating leaf in the tomato meristem, whereas growth is much higher on the opposing abaxial side.
source: The DR5 maximum tends to be on the adaxial side of the initiating leaf, whereas growth is much higher on the opposing abaxial side.
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis.

claim: The observation that DR5 is high on the adaxial side while growth is high on the abaxial side supports the idea that auxin acts as a trigger for primordium initiation rather than via controlling growth rates directly.
source: This supports the idea that auxin acts as a trigger for primordium initiation (Reinhardt et al., 2003; Smith et al., 2006)⁠ rather than via controlling growth rates directly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data supported by citations.

claim: In 2D or on 2.5D surfaces, local directions can be fully defined by a single distance measure by taking one direction aligned with the gradient of the distance field or a Bezier curve, and the other perpendicular to the first.
source: In 2D or on 2.5D surfaces, local directions can be fully defined by a single distance measure by taking one direction aligned with the gradient of the distance field or a Bezier curve, and the other perpendicular to the first.
evidence: This describes how directions are defined in the software for 2D/2.5D cases.

claim: The method of defining directions in MorphoGraphX is similar to methods used to specify directions in developmental modeling in plants.
source: This is similar to the methods used to specify directions in developmental modeling in plants (Green et al., 2010; Kennaway and Coen, 2019; Kierzkowski et al., 2019; Kuchen et al., 2012; Whitewoods et al., 2020)⁠
evidence: This is a comparison to modeling methods supported by citations.

claim: In 3D, a third direction must be defined in addition to the two directions defined in 2D.
source: In 3D, a third direction must be defined (Kennaway and Coen, 2019; Whitewoods et al., 2020)⁠.
evidence: This is a statement about 3D coordinate systems supported by citations.

claim: In MorphoGraphX, the third direction in 3D can be defined by combining the directions defined by different distance measures.
source: In MorphoGraphX, this can be done by combining the directions defined by different distance measures.
evidence: This describes a method implemented in the software.

claim: The 3D Cell Atlas add-on combines several distance measures for radially symmetric structures such as root and hypocotyls.
source: The 3D Cell Atlas add-on (Montenegro-Johnson et al., 2015)⁠ combines several distance measures for radially symmetric structures such as root and hypocotyls.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software add-on with a citation.

claim: The 3D Cell Atlas places a Bezier curve along the center in the longitudinal direction and combines it with a surface mesh to obtain radial directions.
source: A Bezier curve is placed along the center in the longitudinal direction and combined with a surface mesh to obtain radial directions (Figure 4B).
evidence: This describes how the 3D Cell Atlas works, with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: The relative radial coordinate in the 3D Cell Atlas will follow the layer as the root narrows towards the tip.
source: The relative radial coordinate will follow the layer as the root narrows towards the tip.
evidence: This describes a property of the coordinate system.

claim: The relative distance between the central axis and the organ surface can be used to annotate and classify 3D segmented cells in organs with a layered cellular organization.
source: The relative distance between the central axis and the organ surface can then be used to annotate and classify 3D segmented cells in organs with a layered cellular organization.
evidence: This describes a capability of the method.

claim: Figure 4D shows classification of layers with relative coordinates on an Arabidopsis root.
source: Figure 4D shows classification of layers with relative coordinates on an Arabidopsis root (Montenegro-Johnson et al., 2015)⁠.
evidence: This references a figure showing layer classification with a citation.

claim: Figure 4C shows layer classification using absolute distance from a surface mesh, which can be used as a starting point for layer classification in any organ.
source: Figure 4C shows layer classification using absolute distance from a surface mesh (Montenegro-Johnson et al., 2019)⁠, which can be used as a starting point for layer classification in any organ.
evidence: This references a figure showing layer classification with a citation.

claim: Moving along the PD axis from 0 to 260 μm in the Arabidopsis ovule, variations in cell volume were found with a clear minimum at around 100 μm and a steady increase towards proximal and distal end.
source: Moving along the PD axis from 0 to 260 μm, we found variations in cell volume with a clear minimum at around 100 μm and a steady increase towards proximal and distal end (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Measuring the length, width, and depth of cells separately in the Arabidopsis ovule revealed the underlying cause for differences in cell volume between different PD regions of the outermost integument layer.
source: Measuring the length, width, and depth of cells separately revealed the underlying cause for differences in cell volume between different PD regions of the outermost integument layer.
evidence: This describes the analysis performed to understand cell volume differences.

claim: At the proximal end (at 0 μm) of the Arabidopsis ovule, the cell shape is relatively isotropic with similar values in cell length, width, and depth.
source: At the proximal end (at 0 μm), the cell shape is relatively isotropic with similar values in cell length, width, and depth.
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis.

claim: Moving along the PD axis in the Arabidopsis ovule, cell anisotropy slowly increased, first mostly due to decreasing depth and width (until around 100 μm), later mainly due to increased cell length (from about 150 μm).
source: Moving along the PD axis, cell anisotropy slowly increased, first mostly due the decreasing depth and width (until around 100 μm), later mainly due to the increased cell length (from about 150 μm).
evidence: This is an observation from data analysis.

claim: The increased cell length in the Arabidopsis ovule suggests a highly anisotropic growth along the longitudinal axis in this area.
source: The increased cell length suggests a highly anisotropic growth along the longitudinal axis in this area.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed cell length data.

claim: A potential proliferative region could be suspected in the region between 100 and 150 μm in the Arabidopsis ovule, where cell volume and length are the smallest.
source: A potential proliferative region could be suspected in the region between 100 and 150 μm, where cell volume and length are the smallest.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed cell size data.

claim: Plant organs typically emerge as primordia consisting of undifferentiated tissue.
source: Plant organs typically emerge as primordia consisting of undifferentiated tissue.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in plant developmental biology.

claim: Cells subsequently differentiate, acquiring a unique identity that depends on their location within the organ, via genetic processes that integrate spatial and environmental cues.
source: Cells subsequently differentiate, acquiring a unique identity that depends on their location within the organ, via genetic processes that integrate spatial and environmental cues.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in plant developmental biology.

claim: Although cell differentiation is ultimately controlled by differential gene expression, it is often the case that cell fate can be predicted by geometry, even at very early stages.
source: Although cell differentiation is ultimately controlled by differential gene expression, it is often the case that cell fate can be predicted by geometry, even at very early stages (Yoshida et al., 2014)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yoshida et al., 2014.

claim: It is rare that cells with different cell types have identical morphological features.
source: It is rare that cells with different cell types have identical morphological features.
evidence: This is a general observation about cell morphology and cell type.

claim: MorphoGraphX supports a large variety of measures to quantify different features of cell morphology.
source: MorphoGraphX supports a large variety of measures to quantify different features of cell morphology, including simple geometric measures (area, volume, perimeter, surface area, min and max axis), shape quantifiers (convexity, circularity, lobeyness, largest empty circle, aspect ratio), neighborhood measures (number of neighbors, variability), gene expression (average, total, near boundary), and cell network measures (betweenness centrality, betweenness current flow).
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the software.

claim: Most measures in MorphoGraphX can be used on time-lapse data to quantify changes over time.
source: Most measures can be used on time-lapse data to quantify changes over time (growth rates, gene expression changes, cell proliferation).
evidence: This describes a capability of the software.

claim: The modular architecture of MorphoGraphX allows custom measures tailored to specific problems to be easily added through its plug-in interface.
source: The modular architecture of the software also allows custom measures tailored to specific problems to be easily added through its plug-in interface.
evidence: This describes a design feature of the software.

claim: MorphoGraphX uses a standardized attribute system to store and visualize cell data for both scalar values and tensor (directional) information.
source: Here, the development of more complex data-flows is enabled by the use of a standardized attribute system to store and visualize cell data for both scalar values and tensor (directional) information.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software architecture.

claim: MorphoGraphX has several methods to assign secondary labels to classify cell types and layers.
source: MorphoGraphX has several methods to assign these labels to classify cell types and layers.
evidence: This describes a capability of the software.

claim: Labels in MorphoGraphX can be assigned manually by interactively selecting cells or by employing processes that use heat map measure data to assign secondary labels.
source: These labels can be assigned manually by interactively selecting cells or by employing a number of processes that use heat map measure data to assign secondary labels (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This describes methods available in the software with reference to figures.

claim: Since cells of a common biological cell type have similarities in one or more geometrical, positional, or gene expression attributes, the values of these attributes will often form a cluster, facilitating their automatic classification.
source: Since cells of a common biological cell type have similarities in one or more geometrical, positional, or gene expression attributes, the values of these attributes will often form a cluster, facilitating their automatic classification.
evidence: This is a logical inference about cell type classification based on attribute clustering.

claim: The 3D Cell Atlas add-on for MorphoGraphX clusters cells by relative radial distance and cell size to classify the cell layers of the root, hypocotyl, mature embryo, or other radially symmetric plant organs.
source: An example can be seen in the 3D Cell Atlas add-on for MorphoGraphX (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C, Montenegro-Johnson et al., 2015)⁠ that clusters cells by relative radial distance and cell size to classify the cell layers of the root, hypocotyl, mature embryo, or other radially symmetric plant organs.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software add-on with a figure reference and citation.

claim: MorphoGraphX offers a 2D interactive heat map where information from two independent measures can be visualized and clusters selected.
source: To aid in optimizing cell clustering, MorphoGraphX offers a 2D interactive heat map, where information from two independent measures can be visualized, and clusters selected (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes a feature of the software with figure references.

claim: Multifeature classification tasks can be solved automatically by machine learning approaches when provided with sufficient training data.
source: Multifeature classifications tasks can be solved automatically by machine learning approaches (Cortes and Vapnik, 1995)⁠ when provided with sufficient training data.
evidence: This is a statement about machine learning supported by a citation.

claim: Support vector machines (SVMs) have been used to classify cell types based on geometrical features of plant cells.
source: Of particular relevance are support vector machines (SVMs) that have been used to classify cell types based on geometrical features of plant cells (de Reuille and Ragni, 2017; Sankar et al., 2014)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies using SVMs for cell classification.

claim: MorphoGraphX provides a simple interface to the libSVM SVM library.
source: MorphoGraphX provides a simple interface to the libSVM SVM library (Chang and Lin, 2011)⁠.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software with a citation to the library.

claim: Any cell attribute or measure that can be quantified in MorphoGraphX can be used by the SVM classifier.
source: Any cell attribute or measure that can be quantified in MorphoGraphX can be used by the classifier.
evidence: This describes a capability of the SVM interface in the software.

claim: Once trained on a small group of cells with the desired measures, the SVM classifier can be used to classify all the cells in a sample.
source: Once trained on a small group of cells with the desired measures, the classifier can be used to classify all the cells in a sample (Figure 4H).
evidence: This describes how the SVM classifier works with reference to Figure 4H.

claim: After manual curation, the SVM classification can be used as additional training data, improving the power of the classifier.
source: After manual curation, the classification can then be used as additional training data, improving the power of the classifier.
evidence: This describes an iterative improvement process for the classifier.

claim: The Arabidopsis gynoecium consists of the lateral valve tissues that are fused to the replum.
source: Figure 4G and H and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and G show the cell types of the Arabidopsis gynoecium, which consists of the lateral valve tissues that are fused to the replum.
evidence: This is a statement of plant anatomy with figure references.

claim: Within the valve of the Arabidopsis gynoecium, stomata are homogeneously distributed, consistent with the uniform growth and differentiation of this tissue.
source: Within the valve, stomata are homogeneously distributed, consistent with the uniform growth and differentiation of this tissue.
evidence: This is an observation about stomata distribution.

claim: No stomata cells can be found within the replum of the Arabidopsis gynoecium, which is made up of smaller, more homogeneously sized cells.
source: In contrast, no stomata cells can be found within the replum, which is made up of smaller, more homogenously sized cells.
evidence: This is an observation about cell types in the replum.

claim: Cell typing the Arabidopsis gynoecium can be useful to identify the region of the valve margin, where the fully matured fruit will dehisce to release the seeds.
